As a Field Service Engineer, you'll work with state-of-the-art power technologies, delivering installation, commissioning, maintenance, troubleshooting, and digital service solutions that keep critical infrastructure running efficiently. If you're looking for a role that combines technical expertise, customer engagement, travel opportunities, and continuous professional development, this is your chance to make a lasting impact while growing your career with a world-class organization.
q: Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
3 to 5 years of experience in field service, installation, commissioning, maintenance, testing, or related engineering activities.

r: Perform installation, commissioning, maintenance, testing, troubleshooting, repair, upgrade, and retrofit activities for power systems, electrical equipment, and service solutions across the Hitachi Energy portfolio.
Execute field service activities in accordance with technical procedures, contractual requirements, and customer expectations.
Provide high-quality technical support both remotely and on-site to resolve customer issues efficiently.
Diagnose electrical, mechanical, control, and protection system faults and implement effective corrective actions.
Conduct preventive, predictive, and condition-based maintenance activities, while recommending improvements to enhance equipment performance, reliability, and lifecycle management.

Prepare accurate service reports, technical documentation, risk assessments, method statements, fault analysis reports, repair records, recommendations, and site documentation in line with company standards.
Build strong customer relationships and identify opportunities for service agreements, upgrades, modernization projects, digital solutions, spare parts, and refurbishment initiatives.
Collaborate closely with Sales, Project Management, Supply Chain, and other stakeholders to support customer requirements and contribute to business growth.
Travel to customer sites locally and internationally, as required.
Provide timely support for critical service issues and customer escalations to help ensure the reliable operation of customer assets.
Comply with all applicable health, safety, environmental, quality, and regulatory requirements.
Demonstrate Hitachi Energy's values of safety and integrity in all aspects of work.

The Postal Finance Clerk supports daily postal finance operations for ASAB, ADAB, Optional AUAB, and MSAB locations. This role processes and reconciles postal transactions using USPS POS/RSS or an equivalent postal financial system. The clerk maintains accurate financial records, safeguards accountable funds and stock, prepares required reports, and ensures compliance with USPS policies, procedures, and internal controls.
Various Locations: Ali Al Salem Air Base (ASAB), Kuwait; Al Dhafra Air Base (ADAB), United Arab Emirates; Muwaffaq Salti Air Base (MSAB), Jordan; optional placement at Al Udeid Air Base (AUAB), Qatar

A government contract requires that this position be restricted to U.S. citizens or legal permanent residents. You must provide documentation that you are a U.S. citizen or legal permanent resident to qualify.
Estimated Starting Salary Range for Postal Finance Clerk: TBD
Full time benefits include Medical, Dental, Vision, 401K and other possible benefits as provided. Benefits are subject to change with or without notice.
r: Process postal retail and financial transactions accurately using USPS POS/RSS or an equivalent postal financial system.
Reconcile daily financial activity, including cash, money orders, stamps, accountable paper, retail transactions, and other postal revenue.
Prepare, review, and maintain daily, weekly, and monthly financial reports and supporting documentation.
Identify, research, and resolve discrepancies, shortages, overages, and transaction errors in a timely manner.
Maintain financial records in accordance with USPS requirements, contract requirements, and established internal controls.
Safeguard cash, stamps, money orders, accountable items, and other postal assets.
Support audits, inspections, inventory counts, and financial reviews by providing accurate records and documentation.
Coordinate with postal personnel, site leadership, and customers to resolve finance-related issues.
Assist with administrative tasks related to postal operations, including filing, data entry, reporting, and records retention.
Follow all applicable security, privacy, safety, and ethical standards while handling postal and financial information.
Perform other duties as assigned in support of postal finance operations at ASAB, ADAB, Optional AUAB, and MSAB.
Postal Finance Clerk Experience, Education, Skills, Abilities requested:
Minimum of two (2) years of experience using USPS POS/RSS or an equivalent postal financial system.
Demonstrated experience processing, balancing, reconciling, and reporting financial transactions.
Working knowledge of postal financial procedures, accountable property controls, and cash-handling practices.
Ability to identify and resolve financial discrepancies with accuracy and attention to detail.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel, Word, and Outlook.
Ability to maintain accurate records and handle sensitive financial information with discretion.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Ability to work independently and as part of a team in a fast-paced operational environment.
Ability to meet all applicable access, security, background screening, and deployment requirements for the assigned work location.
Prior experience supporting USPS operations in an overseas, remote, military, or contingency environment.
Experience supporting postal operations at ASAB, ADAB, AUAB, MSAB, or similar locations.
Experience with USPS financial reporting, audits, inspections, and accountable paper inventory.
Knowledge of USPS retail systems, postal regulations, and standard operating procedures.
Experience working with government contracts or Department of Defense customers.
Associate degree or higher in accounting, finance, business administration, or a related field.

q: Individuals who will strive to deliver valuations on time and within budget will do well in this environment. Bachelor's degree in finance, economics, accounting, or business.
At least 7 years of valuation work experience with Oil and Gas/Energy clients with a significant part spent working at a Big 4.
Experience managing valuation projects for M&A, Purchase Price Allocations, and Fair Valuations.
Financial modeling skills, including building and reviewing models for Energy businesses.
Proven ability to write and own valuation reports for M&A and Financial Reporting.
r: As a Valuations Manager, you'll be working on large Oil and Gas clients delivering valuations and modelling projects to high standards. You will also be engaged in driving growth through business development and active solution positioning.
You'll perform valuations and modelling assignments, as well as being involved in drafting presentations and reports, formulating views, presenting conclusions to client and teams.
Have hunger to grow and develop professionally.
Have valuation experience in a professional services/Big 4 firmand working with large clients.
Have commercial drive and hunger for business development
Made progress towards a CFA, CA, or other professional qualification.

We are looking for candidates who are highly motivated, analytical, logical thinkers with a passion for valuations and have a very strong attention to detail. Being a strong team player is critical with the ability to adapt to changing requirements or deadlines in support of our clients goals.
